findings.title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new second branch of the deleteMany OR clause is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. This means any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount ever exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron, regardless of its scheduledDate. Today only this handler increments retryCount so the blast radius is limited, but the query no longer matches its stated purpose ('delete all scheduled sms reminders...'), and as soon as any other code path (e.g. an email retry mechanism) writes retryCount, this cron will silently delete those reminders. The retryCount condition should be ANDed with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

findings.title: retryCount update inside catch block can throw and abort the entire cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` to increment retryCount. If the original error was caused by a database problem (connection loss, timeout), this update will also fail; likewise it throws a P2025 if the reminder row was already deleted (e.g. by a concurrently running cron invocation's deleteMany). Because the await sits directly in the catch handler with no nested try/catch, the exception propagates out of the loop, aborts processing of all remaining reminders, and returns a 500. Before this PR the catch only logged, so a single failing reminder was isolated. The increment should be wrapped in its own try/catch (or use a fire-and-forget update with error handling) so one bad reminder cannot kill the whole batch.

findings.title: retryCount incremented via stale read instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both failure paths set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is otherwise updated between read and write), one increment is lost and the reminder gets more retry attempts than the intended two. Prisma supports an atomic update via `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which avoids the read-modify-write race entirely.

findings.title: Comment above deleteMany no longer describes the query
findings.body: The comment 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' still sits above a deleteMany that now also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 (of any method, any scheduledDate). The comment misleads future readers about what the query removes and should be updated to cover the retry-based deletion.
